sections.title: Rounding out the family
sections.content: The same -a/-e/-ja/-je pattern covers the rest of the family. One word changes shape: fiú ("son") shortens to fia ("his/her son") — the vowel-final part of the word just drops before the ending.

items.spanish: Anna fia és lánya is Budapesten van.
items.english: Anna's son and daughter are both in Budapest.

items.spanish: Ez a nagymamája és a nagypapája.
items.english: This is his/her grandmother and grandfather.

sections.content: fiú -> fia is the one to just memorize — it's one of a small handful of Hungarian nouns that shorten before a possessive suffix, and it's common enough that you'll meet it constantly.
